tjam.summary: PROJUDI, one of the main systems for legal proceedings in Amazonas
tjam.intro: The digital judicial process, also called the virtual or electronic process, can be defined as a computer system that reproduces the entire judicial procedure in electronic form, replacing the recording of procedural acts on paper with the storage and handling of case files in digital form.
tjam.lead: I'm working with a legacy system which is passing through an entire migration of technologies to match modern applications.

sections.title: Java
sections.text: Built modular and responsive web applications for the Justice department, leveraging Java's components, based on the requirements of key figures in the judiciary and their demands for the functioning of the system. Projudi is very simple and secure to use. Lawyers and citizens who wish to file a complaint with the Special Courts can use the Internet or go to the courts' service desk. These requests are recorded electronically, with automatic distribution and registration of the case. From then on, all acts are performed using the computer, eliminating the use of paper.

summary: Contributing to PROJUDI, the electronic judicial process system of the Amazonas Court of Justice, during its migration to modern technologies.

gesin.summary: A State Department of Education in Amazonas
gesin.intro: The creation of the State Department of Education (SEDUC) occurred in 1946 through Law 1,596, dated January 5, 1946, initially named the General Directorate of the Department of Education and Culture. With Law 12, dated May 9, 1953, the first change in its nomenclature occurred, and it was renamed the Department of Education, Culture, and Health. Later that same year, under Law 65, dated July 21, 1953, it was renamed the Department of Education, Health, and Social Assistance. Two years later, under Law 108, dated December 23, 1955, it was named the Department of Education and Culture. Another change occurred 36 years later, with Law 2,032, dated May 2, 1991, when it was renamed the State Department of Education, Culture, and Sports. The current name, State Department of Education and Quality of Teaching (SEDUC), was established by Law 2,600, dated February 4, 2000.

projects.intro: Personal projects I build in my free time.

guild.goal: Run several coding agents at once while keeping every decision and every merge.
guild.motivation: One agent is easy to follow. Several agents at the same time are not: you lose track of what each one does and what it decided for you. Guild gives each agent its own worktree and tab, and puts every real choice on a local page so I decide, not the agent. All state stays in plain files on my machine.
goals: Plans approved before any code is written
Acceptance checks written first and sealed
An independent review before every pull request
Decisions on a local page instead of in chat
All state in plain files on your own machine
images: Guild war table: a plan page with steps and acceptance checks (demo data)
Guild campaign board: quests moving from to-do to done (demo data)
Guild wrap-up page with trial evidence and numbers (demo data)
guild.note: The code is public on GitHub but has no license yet: it is a personal tool, not an open source product.

claude-deck.goal: One terminal screen to watch every Claude Code session across all your accounts.
claude-deck.motivation: When several Claude Code sessions run in different terminal tabs and accounts, it is hard to know which one is working, which one is waiting, and what each one costs. claude-deck reads Claude Code's own local files, so it needs no API key and sends nothing over the network.
goals: See live and recent sessions from all accounts in one list
Show each session's agent tree, tasks and cost
Read a colored transcript and send a message to a live session
Jump to the right terminal tab, or mirror its screen
Pin the conversations you care about and resume past ones
images: claude-deck dashboard with conversations, agent tree, tasks and stats (mock data)
claude-deck with pinned conversations at the top (mock data)
claude-deck colored transcript with a message box (mock data)

sr-automation.goal: An LLM pipeline that screens, extracts and summarizes papers for systematic reviews.
sr-automation.motivation: This is the code of my master's dissertation in software engineering. A systematic review means reading hundreds of papers by hand. The project tests how far an LLM can do the first steps, and how to check its answers against a human gold standard.
goals: Collect papers for a query and a range of years
Screen each paper with a YES or NO answer
Extract structured data from the papers kept
Write a three-sentence summary for each paper
Measure recall, precision, F1 and Cohen's Kappa against a human review
images: Pipeline diagram: corpus, screening, extraction, summary
SR-Automation web page with the ten pipeline steps

search-engine-c.goal: A search engine written in C for historical documents of the Amazon region, stored locally.
search-engine-c.motivation: This was an information retrieval course project. It builds the parts of a search engine by hand: a vocabulary with a hash table, an inverted list, and a ranking of documents by how similar they are to the query.
goals: Build a vocabulary of all terms in the documents
Build an inverted list that maps each term to its documents
Weight terms with TF and IDF
Rank documents by similarity to the query
Run on a local collection of 35 historical texts
images: Terminal output of a real search over historical documents of the Amazon region

my-neovim.goal: My Neovim setup for web development, built on LazyVim.
my-neovim.motivation: I wanted an editor that lives in the terminal and that I can keep in a repo. It started from the LazyVim starter template, then I added the tools for web work and, later, Java debugging and Git conflict handling.
goals: Keep the whole editor setup in one repo
Set up the tools for web development
Add Java debugging (DAP)
Handle Git conflicts inside the editor
Work fully from the terminal
